modality_independent_principles: Match information emphasis to user risk, consequence, and decision context.

Make personalization inspectable and controllable by naming the signal or basis, separating recommendations from recent and saved content, and retaining direct search, category, history, notification, and library controls.

Offer retention alternatives only when they genuinely map to a user need and disclose their effect on charges, access, holdings, orders, progress, and future cancellation; keep cancellation visible and independently available.

Name audience reach in concrete terms and explain moderation or participation consequences, distinguishing who can view, who can comment, who can reuse, where copies are saved, and where content is distributed.

Structure B2B onboarding around the operating model and accountable outcomes: separate identity, data connection, workspace structure, security, billing, member invitation, customization, and the first assigned or completed unit of real work.

Make administrative scope explicit across organization, workspace, product, team, and individual levels, showing effective policy, role, authentication, member or seat population, entitlement, save state, and audit history together.

Represent assignment, discussion, state change, dependency, approval, notification, subscription, and completion as different mechanisms with accountable actors and lifecycle; activity alone must not imply ownership or completion.
Explain regulated data requests in plain language by naming what is collected, why it is necessary, and what the user will do next.
Keep clinical measurements self-describing through name, value, unit, reference range, time, trend, source, and interpretation, separating educational context from individualized medical advice.
Separate patient-reported behavior, observed symptoms, clinician-authored findings, automated interpretation, and completed-care claims so one evidence class cannot silently stand in for another.
Treat consent as an inspectable agreement tied to the service, disclosure, signer, date, modality, data use, and withdrawal or support path rather than as an unexplained checkbox.
Support comparison through aligned decision fields, stable units, definition help, variant equivalence, and visible differences rather than forcing memory across product pages.
Make the checkout total reconstructable from items, quantities, discounts, delivery, service charges, regulatory fees, tax, tip, deposits, subscriptions, and temporary authorization.
Treat fulfillment and return as explicit lifecycles with current stage, next expected event, deadline, affected item, amount, payment destination, tracking, support, and safe cancellation.
Distinguish followed, searched, saved, editorial, sponsored, trending, and recommended content, exposing enough source and rationale for users to understand why an item entered the feed.
Name publication reach and participation consequences concretely so viewers, commenters, reusers, community members, and external destinations are not collapsed into one public state.

Make creator economics reconstructable through audience source, active and paid members, trials, conversions, cancellations, tier changes, revenue, payout state, and the content or offer that produced each result.
At booking review, preserve the exact itinerary, traveler identity, operator, segment, baggage, ticket relationship, amendability, refundability, fees, add-ons, payment, currency, and final total.

Treat delay, cancellation, schedule change, missed connection, and supplier cancellation as distinct states with source, last update, affected segment, time consequence, and accountable recovery party.
Build trip continuity around a time-zone-aware sequence of transport, lodging, activities, check-in, documents, local details, and support rather than a disconnected reservation archive.
Separate effort, continuity, mastery, completion, assessment, and credential state so time spent or streak length cannot stand in for learning outcome.

At enrollment, preserve program outcome, format, instructor or authority, start and end timing, cadence, prerequisites, capacity or learner scope, price, discounts, tax, cancellation, and total commitment.

Make instructional analytics actionable by connecting aggregate completion or score to individual learners, assignment state, last activity, due state, evidence, and a proportionate intervention route.
Make observability reconstructable from environment, version, time window, request or trace identity, model or service, latency, cost, usage, errors, tool calls, feedback, and raw drilldown.
Treat prompts and agent configuration as versioned artifacts binding model, instructions, variables, tools, parameters, datasets, evaluators, sharing scope, and deployment state.
Before agent or automation rollout, expose audience, trigger, tools, data scope, permissions, unresolved-case behavior, expected affected population, human review, go-live state, and rollback route.
Lead with a distinctive, decision-relevant point of view and immediately clarify the audience, business situation, or transformation it applies to; do not ask a slogan to carry the full proposition.
Describe each capability through the business change, mechanism, and boundary it addresses rather than presenting an undifferentiated inventory of consulting deliverables.
Treat thought leadership as inspectable intellectual evidence: identify the question or audience, format, date, author or expert, evidence basis, and a concise reason the finding matters now.
Structure client impact around the client context, challenge, intervention, and resulting outcome, attaching metrics to timeframe and comparison basis instead of relying on logos or isolated numbers.

Keep point of view, capability architecture, client proof, intellectual property, expert profiles, and engagement language mutually reinforcing so the corporate story does not fragment into unrelated content systems.

applicability: all supported sections and multi-step flows
modality_independent_principles: Sequence information around orientation, decision, consequence, and recovery.
Establish relevance by naming the audience or situation and the concrete outcome before introducing supporting detail.
Sequence evidence according to the claim and decision risk, using adoption proof, quantitative support, process detail, or safeguards where each is relevant.
Preserve the promised outcome and included value at the point where the user chooses a plan, trial, signup, or upgrade.
State the full commitment model before the action, including price basis, cadence, immediate charge, trial transition, renewal, and material tax or cancellation conditions.
Explain the immediate benefit or necessity before requesting personal data, permissions, or effort.
Present the full cost as a reconstructable equation that updates when taxes, fees, discounts, tips, add-ons, quantities, or fulfillment choices change.
Carry material fulfillment, eligibility, cancellation, and refund consequences into final review instead of leaving them only at discovery.

Organize the dashboard around current state, unresolved consequence, and the next meaningful decision, placing urgent eligibility, incident, risk, overdue, or failed-work signals above descriptive totals and secondary exploration.
Attach each headline measure to its comparison basis, target, denominator, composition, or trend so the value communicates direction and significance rather than a context-free snapshot.
Distinguish healthy zero, empty result, missing data, stale data, excluded scope, not configured, and no recent activity; each state should explain what is known and the most useful next step.

Keep the active query, category, location, date, audience, and other material scope visible beside the results, representing applied constraints as removable state so users can explain, narrow, or broaden the set without reconstructing the search.

Expose the attributes that determine choice at result level, including price basis, availability, eligibility, source, recency, location, scope, or commitment cost, and align comparable fields so users do not have to open every item to judge fit.

Separate retrieval modes such as recent, saved, popular, editorially curated, sponsored, personalized, and query-matched results, and disclose the rationale closely enough that familiarity, payment, or recommendation does not masquerade as relevance.

applicability: draft, review, publish, activate, and export flows
modality_independent_principles: Keep artifact identity, editable draft state, save or sync status, and consequential release state visibly distinct, using a review boundary before publish, activate, send, share broadly, deploy, or export.
Attach validation to the exact field, node, step, asset, audience, or output setting that blocks progress, explain the consequence, and provide a direct route to repair before the release action.

At release, summarize output scope, audience or access, timing, quality, destination, ownership, restrictions, and irreversible or costly consequences, then show progress and a recoverable result state.

Keep collaboration anchored to the exact artifact, object, passage, task, message, source evidence, or version under discussion, preserving author, time, location, and current state so feedback cannot drift from its subject.

Represent discussion, assignment, state transition, decision, approval, and permission as distinct record types with their own owners and lifecycle; a comment, reaction, or personal done state must not imply team completion or authorization.

Make handoffs explicit through one accountable owner, required outcome, due or review condition, dependency and source context, notification scope, and acceptance state, retaining the conversation as evidence rather than as the task itself.

Identify the setting's subject and scope before the control, distinguishing personal, workspace, organization, product, environment, audience, and inherited policy so users know who and what will change.

Explain the operational consequence beside each material control, including visibility audience, notification event and channel, billing commitment, authentication reach, integration data flow, or accessibility behavior.

Separate reversible preference changes from consequential security, privacy, ownership, billing, publication, and deletion actions, using stronger review, authorization, and confirmation in proportion to impact.
Name the requester, granting identity, resource owner, and destination before asking for access, distinguishing a person, application, service, group, administrator, and external party.

Describe permissions as concrete data reads, writes, actions, exports, downloads, comments, edits, administration, billing, or impersonation capabilities, separating independently optional scopes to support least privilege.
State duration and lifecycle explicitly through one-time, while-in-use, ongoing, pending, expiring, deactivated, or revoked status, and provide the later review and revocation path at grant time.

applicability: uploads, imports, synchronization, and background jobs
modality_independent_principles: Classify the state before designing it: distinguish first use, healthy zero activity, zero results under a query or filter, unavailable data, access restriction, validation failure, transient failure, and partial completion so the explanation and recovery match the actual condition.
State what happened, which object or step is affected, and the known cause in operational language; when the cause is unknown, say what is known without replacing uncertainty with a generic message.

For consequential retries, disclose whether the prior action completed, failed before commitment, may still be pending, or affected only a subset; prevent ambiguous repeated submissions and preserve a receipt or diagnostic reference when outcome is uncertain.

Model the corporate website as a multi-audience information system: identify the primary business audience, then provide explicit routes for customers, partners, investors, media, candidates, communities, and existing users without giving every audience equal top-level weight.

Keep a stable institutional hierarchy across header, homepage, footer, search, and subsites, using the same language for products or capabilities, solutions, industries, resources, company, and audience-specific destinations.

Make newsroom, sustainability, governance, and impact content inspectable through date, reporting period, category, metric definition, accountable contact, archive continuity, and a route to the underlying report or release.
Use a consistent expressive hierarchy without allowing style to hide meaning.

Establish an explicit editorial hierarchy with one lead idea or story, a bounded supporting set, and a separate route into the broader archive; do not make every item compete at the same visual level.

Treat headline, deck, category or format, author or publisher, date, and reading scope as one orientation system, keeping the metadata close enough to the story that it cannot be mistaken for another item.
Vary card size or composition only when it communicates a real difference in priority, format, or reading path; preserve a stable content grammar for comparable items.

Create premium expression through selective emphasis: establish one focal product, promise, or experience, then preserve visible orientation, evidence, and action rather than equating scarcity of information with exclusivity.

Turn material and craft into inspectable evidence by connecting close imagery to process, provenance, finish variation, durability, technical specification, compatibility, or the qualities the buyer will receive.

Keep price, duration, billing cadence, included benefits, eligibility, fulfillment, cancellation, and material limitations legible at the commitment boundary; premium presentation must not make the transaction less inspectable.
Create calm through controlled attention by establishing one dominant status, decision, or starting action before styling secondary content.
Reduce visual competition by establishing one dominant task or state, a small number of stable regions, restrained accents, and generous separation while keeping operational meaning explicit.
Treat state as essential content: preserve progress, selection, validation, save or publish status, success feedback, urgency, and recovery even when the surrounding interface is sparse.
Assign expressive elements a job—explain a mental model, motivate progress, identify a content category, or create a focal action—and remove ornament that competes with task comprehension.
Use consistent image treatment, typography, tags, and navigation to turn varied expressive content into a coherent system.
Layer dense work from current health or outcome to trends, exceptions, contributing dimensions, and raw evidence so users can scan first and drill down without losing context.
Separate inputs, assumptions, calculations, outputs, and comparisons visually and semantically; never rely on position or color alone to communicate data role.

Make technical scope persistent by naming project, environment, service, resource, region, version, time range, live state, permission, and secret boundary wherever actions or evidence depend on them.
Use technical density to expose causality and control, not to signal expertise: labels, units, status, exact scope, copyable commands, and safe defaults must remain understandable to a new operator.
Give play a functional role: reduce anxiety, explain a concept, reinforce progress, celebrate a verified result, distinguish identity, or invite the next safe action.
Bind celebration to an inspectable outcome through the completed behavior, achievement condition, earned value, progress count, or next milestone; animation alone must not imply success.
Bind every cinematic hero to decision context through identity, source, metadata, suitability, scope, and a concrete action rather than relying on atmosphere alone.
For consequential or emotional experiences, connect imagery to provenance, measurable state, safeguards, exact commitment, and recovery so emotion cannot substitute for evidence.
Organize the interface around the current object, scope, state, and next operation; use direct labels and stable regions before adding summaries or personality.
At destructive, automated, or costly boundaries, name the affected scope, consequence, run or save state, cost or resource use, history, cancel or stop, and recovery.
Order messages so claims, evidence, tradeoffs, and actions remain distinguishable.
Lead with a recognizable user outcome or completed state before naming the product category, technology, or company ambition.
Make the value concrete by naming the relevant input, task, change, or result closely enough that the intended audience can judge whether it applies.
Follow the outcome immediately with the mechanism that produces it, using process detail, workflow structure, or a legible product state rather than assertion alone.

Name the evidence type and keep it distinct: a product state demonstrates mechanism, a customer result demonstrates an observed outcome, a benchmark demonstrates comparison, an assurance demonstrates control, and a testimonial demonstrates attributed experience.

Make quantitative proof self-describing by attaching the measured outcome to the actor or population, intervention or product use, timeframe, baseline or comparator, unit, and source needed to judge the number.
Preserve uncertainty and transferability limits: identify when evidence comes from one customer, selected examples, commissioned research, a particular dataset, or a specific operating context.

applicability: all supported design reviews and directions
modality_independent_principles: Review hierarchy, comprehension, accessibility, trust, content, and differentiation in the target modality.
Reserve the strongest emphasis for the current state, unresolved consequence, or next meaningful action rather than greetings, tutorials, upgrades, or generic recommendations.
Separate orientation, state, evidence, decision, and secondary exploration through stable regions, spacing, type, order, and contrast instead of relying on one signal alone.
Use consistent form for comparable items and vary size, color, position, or persistence only when the semantic priority or consequence is genuinely different.

Build an explicit semantic definition around important information: name the object, define the measure or status, state scope and time basis, identify source and freshness, and show ownership or authority before users act on it.

Teach workflows as a causal sequence: explain prerequisites, what each stage produces, who participates, expected timing, current progress, remaining work, and what the next transition will make true.
Translate consequential reviews into the underlying people, resources, dates, money, permissions, and obligations, preserving editability and a preview of the exact artifact before commitment.

Keep task context persistent across search, filters, selection, detail, and action: show the active scope, selected count, current object, saved-versus-temporary state, and the result of each operation without forcing users to reconstruct their place.

Prevent form errors with purpose text, appropriate input controls, examples, sensible inherited defaults, conditional fields, and validation close to the source while preserving every valid value and a usable back path.
When an action affects dependent workflow steps, offer explicit downstream choices and explain what will continue, stop, be canceled, be removed, remain preserved, or become inaccessible.

Keep names, labels, instructions, required or optional status, current values, and errors persistently associated with their controls; placeholders and entered content must not become the only way to identify a field.

Make important visual data redundant through direct labels, values, units, legends, symbols, patterns, ranges, written comparisons, and an inspectable table or list alternative so hue, position, or shape is never the sole carrier of meaning.

Use readable type, sufficient contrast, spacing, clear hierarchy, and controls large enough to identify and activate across dense, dark, bright, and data-rich contexts; de-emphasis must not erase essential instructions or status.
Model interactions as explicit transitions with a source state, trigger, target state, timing, prerequisites, and completion condition so users and builders can predict what an action will make true.

Keep interaction context continuous: preserve the affected object, underlying place, current selection, staged changes, and dismissal or return path while menus, popovers, modals, and command surfaces are open.

Separate optimistic acknowledgement from durable completion: show pending or syncing state after immediate feedback, reconcile partial or failed outcomes, and do not let a success notification contradict unresolved work.

Adapt by semantic priority rather than proportional shrinking: preserve current scope, selected object, essential state, primary action, and safe return first, then collapse, move, or defer secondary navigation, inspectors, metadata, and utilities.

Maintain continuity when a multi-pane workspace becomes a compact sequence by preserving selection, title, project or collection, filters, scroll position, unsaved state, and a predictable back path between list and detail.

Test responsive behavior as content and state combinations, including long labels, many panes, wide tables, keyboard visible, empty and error states, selected rows, open menus, active inspectors, and unsaved work—not only at nominal viewport widths.
At the decision boundary, show the exact actor or account, affected object or resource, destination, amount or data scope, permission, and timing needed to verify what will happen.
State consequences in operational terms, including affected dependencies, irreversibility, cost, duration, eligibility, or resulting state, before the final action is available.
Separate current state, observed evidence, inferred risk, and recommended action so a health summary does not become a stronger claim than its visible basis supports.
Place warnings, qualifications, and material terms beside the decision they govern; use linked detail as supporting evidence rather than a substitute for decision-critical disclosure.

Define visual choices by semantic role—surface, text, action, status, focus, border, chart series, heading, body, spacing, and density—then map modes and brands onto those roles instead of exposing unrelated raw values.
Evolve visual systems through explicit save state, legacy mapping, migration notices, and bounded overrides so existing artifacts and behaviors do not silently change.

Define each component through stable anatomy, named properties, bounded variants, and explicit states so optional content and behavior remain understandable without duplicating near-identical components.
Make layered components communicate trigger or parent context, focus scope, dismissal behavior, action priority, and consequence rather than relying on visual elevation alone.
Layer brand expression onto stable semantic roles and interaction contracts so logos, accents, typography, and imagery can vary without changing meaning, priority, or expected behavior.
Specify how user preference, operating-system preference, product defaults, organization policy, and saved personal choices resolve when they disagree.

Create an explicit publication boundary where proposed system changes have a named scope, rationale, owner, review state, version, release note, and effective audience before downstream consumers receive them.
Treat deprecation as a lifecycle with announcement, affected scope, replacement, compatibility period, migration steps, deadline, support path, and final removal rather than a deleted asset.

Adapt by semantic priority: preserve current scope, selected object, consequential state, primary action, and safe return first; collapse, move, summarize, or defer secondary navigation, inspectors, metadata, and utilities.

When simultaneous panes become a compact sequence, preserve selection, title, parent scope, filters, unsaved state, scroll position, and a predictable back path so layout change does not become context loss.
